transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having just a little trouble at work lately. I really don't want you to think I'm a bad person—I usually get along with everyone and try to do a good job—but I've just been... snapping at people. 

It's really embarrassing to admit. Like, we had this safety meeting the other day, and I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. I feel terrible about it. And now the younger inspectors act like they're scared to ask me anything at all. I hate that I made them feel that way, it's not like me. Is... is that the right kind of thing to talk about here? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed yourself getting upset or snapping at people in other parts of your life, like at home or in social situations?

Well... um... yes, I suppose it has spilled over a little bit outside of work. I really try to leave it at the door, but it's been hard. I actually used to be very involved in our local community theater—I love helping with the sets and costumes—but lately... I've just had to pull back. I couldn't always get through the rehearsals without feeling so overwhelmed, and I didn't want to be a burden or ruin the mood for everyone else. They work so hard, you know? 

And at work... well, it's not just the yelling at the meeting. I feel so awful saying this, but I've missed quite a few shifts recently. And because I've lost my patience with the trainees a few times, management decided it's best if I don't mentor the younger inspectors anymore. Which is fair, I completely understand why they did it, I just... I hate that I let them down. I'm usually so dependable. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound completely awful... I really am trying my best to fix this.
Have you noticed that you're not enjoying the things you used to enjoy, like the community theater work or anything else?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't say I'm not enjoying things anymore. I mean, I still really love the theater and everyone there. They're such a wonderful group of people. It's just... maybe I just haven't had as much energy for it lately? 

I still like the idea of doing it, I just... I don't know, maybe I'm just getting a little older and need more quiet time at home. I definitely don't want you to think I'm depressed or just giving up on my hobbies or anything like that. I still care about those things very much. I just... I haven't quite felt up to participating as much as I used to. Is that... is that normal to feel that way sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so I don't give you the wrong impression.
Have you been feeling down or sad lately, even if it's not something you think about all the time?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or sad. I mean, I have so much to be thankful for, you know? I have a good job, a nice place to live... I really try to focus on the positive things. 

I guess I've just been a little more... tense? Or on edge, maybe. But definitely not sad. I don't sit around crying or feeling sorry for myself, I promise. I try to keep a smile on my face and just push through it. I hope that's okay to say? I just really don't want to come across as someone who complains or isn't grateful for what they have. I'm just... trying to figure out why I've been so irritable lately, that's all.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy, even if you still care about them?

Um... no, I really don't think my interest or the pleasure I get from things has decreased at all. I still get a lot of joy out of my hobbies, even just thinking about them. Like I was saying, the passion is absolutely still there. 

I just... I really don't want you to think I'm losing interest in my life or anything like that. I just get a little worn out from feeling so tense all the time, so I stay home a bit more. But the pleasure is definitely still there when I do things! I hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same sort of answer... I just want to make sure I'm being accurate so I don't waste your time or lead you down the wrong path. Does that make sense?

Can you tell me more about what happens right before you feel yourself getting tense or snapping at others? Is there something specific that tends to set it off, or does it seem to come out of nowhere?

Well, um... it's hard to say exactly what sets it off. I guess it kind of feels like it comes out of nowhere sometimes? I really don't mean to be difficult or mean to anyone, I promise. I'm usually a very patient person. 

But... well, I guess I'm actually here because I keep snapping at people at work. Like... there was this safety meeting recently, and I just... I started yelling before I could even stop myself. It was so out of character for me, and I felt just awful about it afterward. I really didn't mean to make a scene. But now... I think the younger inspectors are scared to ask me anything, and I just hate that they might think I'm this angry person. I really try to be helpful and kind to everyone. I hope you don't think I'm a bad person for losing my temper like that... I'm just trying to understand why I'm acting this way so I can fix it. Is it normal to just snap like that when you're feeling stressed?
Have you been having any physical symptoms lately, like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, feeling restless, or having a hard time concentrating?

Um... well, I really try not to complain about every little thing, you know? I think at my age, and working on my feet as an inspector, a little muscle tension is just part of the job. And I really do try my absolute best to stay focused during my shifts. 

But... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. I almost feel bad even bringing it up, because I know everyone gets tired sometimes and I don't want to sound whiny. It's just... most nights, I lay there and I really can't seem to fall asleep until it's almost dawn. Or, if I do manage to drift off earlier, I end up jerking awake. 

It's usually from these... well, these dreams. They always have the line alarms in them, and this just awful metal sound. It's probably silly to let a dream bother me so much, I know. But even when I do manage to get a few hours of shut-eye, I wake up feeling like I never really slept at all. 

I hope it's alright that I shared that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information so I'm not making your job harder. Does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when you know logically there may not be a reason to be so concerned?

Um... well, no, I wouldn't really say I'm a worrier. I mean, I think it's normal to care about doing a good job and making sure things are done right, especially in my line of work where safety is so important. I just try to be thorough, you know? 

I really don't sit around fretting over things that don't make sense. I've always prided myself on being pretty level-headed and logical. I just... I don't want you to think I'm someone who just panics over nothing. I try to handle whatever comes my way without making a fuss. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how I handle things. Am I making sense?
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or were more irritable than usual for several days in a row?

Oh, um... no, I really don't think so. I'm not the kind of person who gets all wound up like that, I promise. I mean, sure, sometimes I have busy days where I get a lot done around the house or at work, but I think that's just being a hard worker, right? 

I really try to keep an even keel. I don't want you to think I'm running around acting crazy or anything like that. And like I said before, I usually pride myself on being very patient, not irritable... well, except for that one time at work, which I still feel just terrible about. But no, I haven't had days and days of feeling weirdly energetic or not needing sleep. 

I hope I'm answering that right? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and not confusing things. Does that sound like a normal answer to you?
Have you noticed yourself pulling away or avoiding certain activities or people because you're worried you might get too tense or upset around them?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound like I'm not doing my job, because I am. I still go to work every day and do my best. But... I suppose I do go out of my way to not walk past the main inspection bay anymore. It's just... it's easier to take the long way around, you know? I don't want to cause a scene or get upset in front of everyone. 

And... well, if people bring up the accident, I really try to just change the subject. I don't want to bring down the mood or make anyone uncomfortable by talking about it. It's better to just keep things positive, right? 

I also... I used to really love going to these local industrial-history talks. It sounds a bit nerdy, I know, but I found them so interesting. But lately, I just... I stopped going. They show all these pictures of old machinery and... it just kind of sets me off, I guess. I get all tense, and I don't want to be a bother to the people sitting next to me if I start acting jumpy. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound weak or anything, avoiding those things. I just want to keep the peace and not be a burden. Is it okay that I handle it that way? I'm just trying to do what's best so I don't upset anyone else.
Can you tell me more about the accident you mentioned? Have you been feeling upset or having strong reactions when reminded of it?

Oh... um... I really hate to dwell on it, because I wasn't the one who got physically hurt, you know? I don't want to sound like I'm making it all about me, or being dramatic. It was just a really bad accident with one of the machines, and my coworker... well, I was right there doing my inspection when it happened. 

But to answer your question... I guess I do get a little upset sometimes. I try so hard to just push through it and do my job, I really do. But... well, sometimes just a loud clank from a utility cart, or... or if I catch that smell of hot oil... it just puts me right back in that bay. It’s like... I see my coworker by the machine, and it feels like it’s happening in front of me all over again. 

I know it probably sounds silly, because I know I'm safe where I am. I really try to just keep my head down, take a breath, and not let it show so I don't bother anyone else on the floor. I hope that's an okay answer? I just feel so foolish when my mind does that... is it normal to get spooked by little things like that?
Do you ever feel like you're actually reliving the accident, like it's happening all over again in your mind, even when you know you're safe?

Um... yes, I... I think I did mention that just a moment ago, didn't I? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much or being confusing. But yes, that's exactly what happens. 

It's like... if I hear a loud clank from one of the utility carts going by, or if I catch that specific smell of hot oil... it's just awful. It's like I'm not in my current spot anymore. I'm suddenly right back in that bay, and I can see my coworker by the machine, and it feels exactly like it's happening all over again right in front of me. 

I know I'm perfectly safe, and I try so hard to just shake it off and keep working so I don't cause a fuss. I really don't want anyone to think I'm losing my mind or that I can't handle my job. It just takes over for a minute, you know? I hope it's okay that I feel that way... does that make sense to you?
Do you find yourself being easily startled or constantly on guard, even in situations where you know you’re safe?

Um... well... I guess I do, a little bit? I mean, I really try not to be jumpy, because I know it probably looks silly to other people. I don't want anyone to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. 

But... even when I'm just sitting in the break room, or... or even when I'm at my choir rehearsal on the weekends, I find myself doing it. I try to stop, I really do, but I just... I catch myself always watching the doors, you know? And I'm always listening so hard for any sudden machine noises, even when I'm nowhere near the floor. And... I'm constantly checking who's moving behind me. 

It's just like... no matter how much I tell myself I'm fine, my body just won't believe that I'm safe. I really hope that doesn't sound too crazy. I try so hard to hide it so I don't make anyone else nervous. Is it okay that I'm still reacting like that? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting to things.
Do you go out of your way to avoid people, places, or things that remind you of the accident?

Oh... um, well... I really try not to let it interfere with my duties, I promise. I don't want to be difficult or make extra work for anyone. But... I suppose I do, yes. 

I actually go out of my way now so I don't have to pass that specific inspection bay. I take the long way around the floor, which I hope my supervisor doesn't think means I'm wasting time... it just helps me keep my composure so I can do a good job. And... well, I really won't talk about the accident if I can help it. If someone brings it up, I try to just politely change the subject. I don't want to bring the mood down or make anyone else uncomfortable, you know?

I also... well, this feels a bit silly to admit, but I used to really enjoy going to these local industrial-history talks. I actually quit going to them recently. The pictures they show of the old machinery... they just set me off too much now. I feel awful for missing them, but I just don't want to risk getting upset in front of people and making a scene. I hope it's okay that I'm avoiding those things? I just really want to handle this the right way without being a burden.
